architecture.summary: T2: 1 public module added; declarations changed in 3 public modules; 2 registry views added, 5 registry views edited

reasons.fact: S2.5-01b adds organization-owned removal admission, current authority and exact target checks, last-active-Admin protection, and conditional completion. The existing private SQL adapter implements a new public RemovalOperationStore on the same bounded pool, with one pending operation per organization and retained terminal receipts. Uncertain effects remain held without replay. A 30-second owner lifetime and ten-page bound guard dispatch; optional neutral read signals stop further WorkOS read substeps while in-flight calls retain their existing five-second timeout. App supplies and closes the removal owner before shared SQL. Public request/result/store and directory stop contracts are snapshot-visible; invitation results and unrelated callers stay compatible. Organizations and audit-logs gain responsibilities and shared storage/recovery guarantees change, but the component set, source dependency pairs, C4 container topology, provider selection, and runtime configuration remain. Updated registry views describe the new runtime call separately from the existing opposite type dependency. No browser removal route, customer removal export, MFA, or live migration is added. The policy change registers the new public module and extends the existing PostgreSQL gate without weakening checks.

src/accounts/organizations/membership-removal-checks.ts covered by "One rule file keeps current actor authority, exact target facts, all grant support, complete bounded member pages, and the last-Admin decision together. Its largest function has nine paths, covered by refusal, pagination, duplicate, and target-change cases. Per-guard files would hide the order that prevents a stale User-to-Admin transition from bypassing the last-Admin check." until 2026-12-24

src/accounts/organizations/membership-removal-lifetime.ts covered by "One small lifetime owns the total deadline, admission uncertainty, read stop signal, guarded continuations, and one public result. Its largest function has four paths. Tests cover the exact deadline, accumulated phase time, close, late replies, and signal propagation. Splitting timer, stop, or result state into another owner would obscure release-once and no-late-dispatch guarantees." until 2026-12-24

src/accounts/organizations/membership-removal.ts covered by "One removal owner keeps authorization, durable admission, current checks, single dispatch, and conditional terminal receipts in one ordered flow. Its largest function has nine paths. Focused cases cover ambiguous admission, provider uncertainty, completion mismatch, and exact receipt matching. Further splitting would spread the no-replay and completion authority rules without reducing their decisions." until 2026-12-24
